paper.title_en: Role of excited hyperons in $K^{*}Ξ$ production via $K^{-}N$ scattering
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the production mechanism of $K^-N\to K^*Ξ$ and the role of high-mass excited hyperons within an effective Lagrangian approach, using a combined fit to cross section and polarization data for $K^-p\to K^{*+}Ξ^-$. The model includes $s$- and $u$-channel exchanges of the ground-state $Λ$ and $Σ$ hyperons, together with $s$-channel contributions from $Λ(2325)$ and $Σ(2230)$. The pronounced near-threshold enhancement of the total cross section is driven mainly by these excited hyperons, whereas $u$-channel exchange dominates at backward angles at higher energies. Polarization results show that both the $K^*$ spin-density matrix elements and the $Ξ$ recoil polarization are sensitive to excited-hyperon contributions near threshold. Notably, the latter remains sensitive to interference involving excited-hyperon amplitudes even at higher energies. Moreover, with the same fitted parameters and no additional free parameters, the predicted cross sections for $K^-p\to K^{*0}Ξ^0$ and $K^-n\to K^{*0}Ξ^-$ agree well with available measurements. Finally, a Dalitz analysis of $K^-p \to K^{*+}Ξ^- \to KπΞ^-$, together with existing $KπΞ^-$ cross section data, indicates the feasibility of reconstructing $K^{*+}Ξ^-$ through this final state. These results suggest that $K^*Ξ$ production provides a valuable reaction channel for investigating high-mass excited hyperons and their hadronic couplings, and offers theoretical guidance for future experimental measurements.
